main_text.p: mus eius pijs hominibus compleretur, essetque planè Dei Ecclesia.] Insuper, & in Ciuitate erant Olympius Tribunus, & Niceph. Lib.6. Cap. 13.{c} Asterius Senator, claro loco natus, & magno ab Imperatore in pretio habitus, & in exercitu{d} Marinus, unus ex his qui in eo magnum decus & honorem fuissent consecuti, vir & genere illustris, & diuitijs locuples. Illum aliquando è Tribunali egressum, trium tantùm horarum spatio ei ad deliberandum dato, ut vel à religione desisteret, vel in ea perseverans capite plecteretur: Theotectnus Cæsariensis Episcopus ad se colloquendi causa inuitat, & præhensa manu rectâ deducit in Ecclesiam. Quē cùm interiùs ad ipsum Sanctuarium collocauisset, læua paululùm in alte-ram partem dimota, gladium quo cin-gebatur ostendit, simulque diuinorum Euangeliorum librum adferens, ex ad-uerso porrigit. Quotusquisque Mari-anista non statim ex hoc Sermone muto collegisset, voluisse Episcopum ut Ma-rinus suos milites ad defectionem hor-taretur. Euangeliumque contra Impe-ratoris autoritatem, & Edicta, gladio

page.notes: Marginal notes in the left margin: beside "Asterius" the note "c Niceph. Lib.6. Cap. 13."; beside "Marinus" the note "d Euseb. Lib. 7. Cap. 13.", which is printed with a long-s-like f in "Eufeb" and is transcribed as Euseb. The first word of the part is cut at the left edge of the scan, so only "mus" is legible. The catchword "de" is small and partly cut; the reading is doubtful. Long s is written as plain s throughout. The printed "ex hoc" and "ex ad-verso" are set with a narrow space, so I have written them as separate words. "Euangelium" is kept as printed in the text, with u/v normalised to v where it is consonantal.
